plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether physics-aware initialization (quarter-wave Bragg mirrors + half-wave defect cavity) improves convergence over uniform/random starting points for a dual-band IR pass filter. Drawn from recalled thin-film design practice: Bragg stacks create stopbands, defect cavities create transmission peaks. Would have wanted to look up exact n/k dispersion data for ZnS and MgF2 in the 3.5-5.5 μm range to refine quarter-wave calculations.

routes.title: Physics-aware initialized 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 defect-cavity dual-band IR filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses around calculated quarter-wave (Bragg mirror) and half-wave (defect cavity) values with ±5% perturbation will achieve higher best_target_score and maintain tightest_margin compared to uniform or random initialization, because the search begins within the resonant optical path length basin.
routes.design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflectors (alternating high/low index quarter-wave layers) create high-reflectance stopbands. A central defect cavity (half-wave optical thickness) breaks the periodicity and creates transmission peaks within the stopband. For dual-band transmission, the defect region thickness and surrounding mirror symmetry determine peak positions and widths.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers, initialized around physics-calculated quarter-wave and half-wave values with ±5% Gaussian perturbation
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: layer thicknesses should remain within depositable ranges 50-1000 nm
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (t = λ/4n) creates maximum reflectance for Bragg mirrors at design wavelength
Half-wave optical thickness (t = λ/2n) in defect cavity creates transmission resonance within Bragg stopband
Symmetric mirror structures around defect cavity improve peak transmission and reduce sideband ripple
ZnS (high index ~2.3) and MgF2 (low index ~1.35) provide sufficient index contrast for mid-IR Bragg mirrors
Dual transmission peaks can be achieved by tuning defect cavity thickness to support multiple resonant modes
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to physics-aware initialization
Higher best_target_score compared to uniform 100nm starting point
Better preservation of tightest_margin across optimization rounds
known_risks: Refractive index values for ZnS and MgF2 at 4-5 μm are recalled approximations (ZnS ~2.2-2.4, MgF2 ~1.3-1.4); exact dispersion data from registry will determine actual quarter-wave thicknesses
Dual-band transmission with single defect cavity may not achieve both passbands equally; may require asymmetric mirror design or multiple defects
22 layers may not provide sufficient stopband rejection; 24 layers could improve but was not chosen to maintain comparability with prior iteration
Quarter-wave calculation uses single center wavelength (~4.4 μm) but passbands span 4.15-4.75 μm; broadband performance may differ from narrowband design
Daimon-20 substrate dispersion in mid-IR range is recalled but not verified against registry data
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer multilayer infrared filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence at normal angle. Stack sequence: zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2/zns/mgf2 (22 layers total, alternating). Initialize layer thicknesses using physics-aware bootstrap: calculate quarter-wave thickness t = λ_center/(4×n) for Bragg mirror layers using λ_center = 4400 nm and estimated effective indices (zns n≈2.3, mgf2 n≈1.35), calculate half-wave thickness t = λ_center/(2×n) for central defect cavity layers (layers 11-12), then apply ±5% Gaussian perturbation to create initial population. Optimize all 22 individual layer thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in passbands 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm while minimizing mean transmittance in stopbands 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Use coherent thin-film matrix method. Spectral evaluation range 3500-5300 nm. No metal layers. Maximum layer thickness 1000 nm, minimum 50 nm.
routes.revision_reason: Repair material name ambiguity: replaced CaF2 with Daimon-20 substrate per registry resolution requirement. CaF2 matched 4 datasets equally; Daimon-20 is one of the two accepted diagnostic names that pins exactly one dataset.

No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Exact refractive index dispersion for zns and mgf2 at 3.5-5.5 μm must be read from registry dataset, not assumed from recalled values
Whether single defect cavity can achieve two distinct passbands of equal transmission, or if asymmetric mirror design is needed
Optimal number of Bragg pairs on each side of defect (10 pairs used here, but 9+9 or 11+11 might better balance the two passbands)
Daimon-20 substrate optical properties in mid-IR must be confirmed from registry data
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot achieve best_target_score > 0.60 after physics-aware initialization, the fundamental limitation may be the material pair (zns/mgf2) or the 22-layer topology rather than the optimization approach; would need to explore different material combinations or increase layer count toward the 24-layer maximum.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase relative to iteration_04 baseline (0.5777) if physics-aware initialization improves search efficiency
valid_candidates count should remain stable or increase if initialization keeps designs within physically valid parameter space
tightest_margin should not decrease across rounds if physics-aware starting point avoids constraint violations
thicknesses_nm should show bimodal distribution clustering around quarter-wave (~480 nm for zns, ~815 nm for mgf2) and half-wave values rather than uniform 100 nm
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10% and continue
if tightest_margin becomes negative for all candidates in a round, reinitialize with wider ±10% perturbation around physics-calculated values

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
